pairs.why: These are close to identical, but A's lenses and steel read slightly calmer and more matte, while B's glassier lenses and extra coin button add polish and fuss.
B is the cleaner, calmer viewer focused on the pole like the real card, while A adds a busy prop scene, a bolted base, saturated reflective lenses and a glossier toy finish.
A's rounded blue-and-silver housing gives a compact, soft silhouette closer to the real viewer's colour masses, while B leans on a flat steel faceplate with rivets.
B has the calmer, more matte wood and a softer finish, while A pushes a saturated, glossy plastic-toy look beyond the real feeder.
A's simple post-and-plank feeder with a plain plank roof reads closer to the real card than B's arched walls and metal eyelets.
A keeps a clean, readable wooden build, while B adds bolts, a metal hanger plate and a ring, which is fussy mechanical construction the real card doesn't have.
A matches the real card's main colour masses (dark blue body, dark blue keys, cyan operator column), while B's cream keys change the overall look even though they carry printed labels.
A again keeps the real all-blue keypad with cyan accents, while B's large cream keys move the colour masses away from the real calculator.
